C_businessGraph.name: NVIDIA accelerated-computing platform

Current operating capability is represented by durable free-cash-flow generation; future operating potential depends on continued accelerator demand, networking adoption, software mix and the durability of unusually high cash margins.

C_businessGraph.rationale: A normalized DCF is the primary method because the supplied evidence includes a complete FCFF bridge, forward FCF, normalized margins, net cash and a discount-rate policy. Current operating capability is separated from future platform potential through explicit growth and margin constraints. No standalone value is assigned to unbuilt optionality without commercial evidence.

forecastAssumptions.rationale: Use the supplied forward-revenue forecast as the starting point without incorporating market price or valuation targets.
Use supplied forward FCF as the current operating-capability anchor.
Carry the supplied normalized cash-margin assumption while testing durability through explicit margin constraints.
Use the supplied model-family discount-rate policy; it is derived rather than a sourced CAPM estimate.
Use the supplied long-run growth policy without increasing it based on valuation preference.

growthConstraints.rationale: Bound the forecast for technology-cycle and customer-spending cyclicality while preventing unsupported hypergrowth. Company-specific KPI validation is still required.
The current normalized margin may be durable but remains exposed to product-cycle, mix and competitive pressure.
Keep terminal growth at or below the supplied long-run policy because long-run platform growth is not separately evidenced.

forecastYears.note: Capex is embedded in the FCFF basis; zero here means not separately forecast, not zero economic investment.

scenarios.name: Technology-cycle reset
scenarios.description: Customer digestion, competition or mix pressure causes a material revenue-growth and margin reset before normalization.
